approach: Root cause: the pre-verification mirror registry (crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs, run at the producer step by mirror_drift_in in run/producer.rs) never compared a finished prompt file or new decision-log entry with the structure it must keep. Jobs 20261015-095214-y8kr (two bullets joined in reader.md) and 20261025-034452-wqp8 (D122 inserted inside D121) were found only at the final verdict. Fix it in the registry, so the producer loop and the candidate/test gate run it with no new call site. Add two Rule variants and two REGISTRY entries. (1) `PromptStructure`, mirror `crates/*/prompts/*.md` (a glob; new `Mirror::files` and `Mirror::covers` expand and match it), source GitHead. For each prompt file it compares base and new text and reports (a) a base bullet head (`- word:`) that now sits mid-line, i.e. a joined bullet, and (b) a new line, not present in the base, with a second `- word:` marker glued after text. (2) `DecisionEntries`, mirror docs/decisions.md, source GitHead. When the base is a byte prefix of the new text, it judges only entries that start at or after the end of the base: heading shape `## D<n> · title`, id one greater than the previous entry (no duplicate), and a `- **Provenance:**` bullet inside the entry's own span. A decision inserted inside another leaves the outer entry with no Provenance and is named. Legacy entries are never judged. Also make the existing append-only message name the entry that holds the changed base line, so D122-inside-an-existing-D121 is reported as D121 too. The rules judge structure, not intent: the job carries no machine-readable intent, so what is checked is that bullets stay one per line and entries stay whole, which is exactly what the two jobs broke. Prompt files are not edited. xtask/shard-timings.txt needs no change because no new test file is added; tests go into existing files.

decisions.choice: Declare the checks as REGISTRY entries (new Rule variants) in mirrors.rs.
decisions.reason: mirror_drift_in (run/producer.rs:75-86) already calls check_all with the producer's changed paths before the verifier and sends a drift back once through append_mirror_drift; the athena-cli `mirrors` test runs every entry unfiltered over the real tree. A registry entry therefore needs no new call site and fixes the whole class of prompt and decision-log files.

rejected.option: A new check in run/checks.rs or a hook in run_check
rejected.why: It runs after handover, in the verifier's snapshot, where a break can be excused as pre-existing; D158 already rejected this for the same reason.

rejected.option: Only a test in athena-cli (extend decisions.rs check_log)
rejected.why: That is the late stage where the failures were found. check_log (crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs:218) is a private fn in a cfg(test) module and runs only under the full cargo test.

rejected.option: A new call site in producer.rs
rejected.why: Duplicates what mirror_drift_in does and leaves the candidate gate unprotected.

decisions.choice: Allow a glob in Mirror.mirror: add `Mirror::files(root)` (expands a pattern with `*` using the existing segment_matches, otherwise the one file if it exists) and `Mirror::covers(path)`; check_all skips an entry with no files, `watches` uses `covers`, and the PromptStructure drifts name the concrete file.
decisions.reason: A prompt file is its own mirror; the set of roles grows, so a fixed list would go stale. The glob helpers already exist (glob_matches, segment_matches).

rejected.option: One REGISTRY entry per prompt file
rejected.why: New roles and capabilities add prompt files; nothing would find a missing entry (registration is prose-only, per the module doc).

rejected.option: Source::Globs with a single placeholder mirror
rejected.why: The findings must name the edited file, and `watches` charges a producer only for entries it touched; a placeholder would break both.

decisions.choice: Check structure invariants and judge only what the diff adds: for prompts, a base bullet head now mid-line, or a new line with a glued second bullet marker; for the log, only entries starting at or after the end of the base, and only when the base is an exact prefix of the new text.
decisions.reason: The job holds no machine-readable intended edit, so intent cannot be compared. The two jobs broke structure (a joined bullet, an entry split by another), which is checkable. Judging only added lines and entries keeps legacy text from newly failing (the real log has a heading gap at D145, per the comment at decisions.rs:216), and when the base is not a prefix the AppendOnly entry already reports, so findings are not doubled.

rejected.option: Make the producer declare the intended lines and fail on hunks outside them
rejected.why: Needs a new plan or record field and a brief change; out of scope and the briefs have no token headroom.

rejected.option: Judge the whole prompt file and the whole log on every run
rejected.why: Legacy lines and entries would fail, and a producer would be charged with drift it did not make.
Arbitrary; it would flag legitimate rewrites and miss a one-line join.

decisions.choice: Keep athena-cli's check_log and its pin as they are; the new rule duplicates its Provenance, id-order and next-id logic for the uncommitted work tree.
decisions.reason: check_log is test-only code in athena-cli, and athena-core cannot depend on the CLI crate. The pin guards committed history; the new rule guards the producer's work tree against its base. Messages use the same wording (`has no Provenance bullet`, `appears twice`, `one greater than`).

rejected.option: Move check_log into mirrors.rs and make the CLI test call it
rejected.why: Its tests pin exact messages and the pinned-hash logic; the refactor is more risk than this change needs. It can follow later.

decisions.choice: Name the containing entry in append_only_problem's message (`line N of its base version, in D121, is changed or removed`) by scanning the base lines before the first changed byte for the last `## D<n>` heading.
decisions.reason: When the base already holds D121 and D122 is inserted inside it, the base prefix is broken, so the AppendOnly entry is what fires and the DecisionEntries rule stays silent. The message must name D121 for criterion 2 to hold in that case too. The text before `is changed` is extended, and the existing assertions (`line 2`, `body`, `add the new decision after the last line`) still hold.

rejected.option: Make DecisionEntries also judge when the prefix is broken

The backtest parse (crates/athena-cli/src/backtest.rs:79-81) reads every `amends`, `supersedes` and `superseded by`, and each hit must be listed in decision-links.toml. The new id is one greater than D161, as the log guard requires.

rejected.why: The root-cause-and-reversal record is the project convention for each registry change (D158, D160).

steps: Read mirrors.rs sections once more where touched: Rule/Mirror/REGISTRY (lines 33-121), append_only_problem (213), `watches`/`check_entry`/`check_all` (647-749), and the test module helpers (`put`, `clean_tree`, `base_of`, `strings`).

In mirrors.rs add the Rule variants `PromptStructure` and `DecisionEntries` with doc comments, and update the module header to say six rules and that prompt files and new decision entries are compared by structure with the base.

Add `Mirror::files(&self, root) -> Vec<String>` (a pattern with `*` is expanded segment by segment with `std::fs::read_dir` and the existing `segment_matches`, sorted; otherwise the one file when `is_file`) and `Mirror::covers(&self, path) -> bool` (glob_matches for a pattern, else equality). Use them in `check_all` (skip an entry whose `files` is empty) and at the top of `watches` (`paths.iter().any(|c| self.covers(c))`).

Write `pub fn prompt_structure_problems(file: &str, base: Option<&str>, new: &str) -> Vec<String>`. Collect the base's bullet heads (a line that starts with `- `: the text up to and including the first `:` within 40 chars, else its first 24 chars when the line has at least 8). Finding (a): a new line that holds a head at an index after its first non-space char, when the line is not a line of the base. Finding (b): a line of the new text, absent from the base lines, with ` - word:` (letters, digits, space, `_`, `/`, `-`, up to 40 chars, then `:`) at an index > 0, preceded by an alphanumeric or one of `. ! ? ; : ) ] * _ ' "`. Each message starts with the file path, gives the line number and a short quote, and ends with a fix naming `put the old text back` and `so each bullet starts its own line`.

Write `pub fn decision_entry_problems(base: &[u8], new: &[u8]) -> Vec<String>`. Return empty unless `new.starts_with(base)`. Scan the new text by lines with byte offsets for `## D<digits>` headings. For each entry with start >= base.len(): heading shape (`## D<n> · `), duplicate id, id == previous id + 1, and a line starting `- **Provenance:**` inside the span up to the next heading. Messages start with `docs/decisions.md:`, name the entry id, and contain a fix phrase (`add `, `remove `).
Edit `append_only_problem` to add `, in D<n>,` after `of its base version` when a `## D<n>` heading precedes the first changed byte in the base; leave the other text as is.

Wire `check_entry`: before the existing match, `if entry.rule == Rule::PromptStructure { ... }` loops over `entry.files(root)`, reads each file and its base text through `base(file)`, and returns `Drift { mirror: file, message }` per problem; add the arm `(Rule::PromptStructure, _) => Vec::new()` to keep the match exhaustive, with a comment. Add `(Rule::DecisionEntries, _)` using `base(entry.mirror)` and the new file (a missing base gives no findings, as AppendOnly does). Add the two REGISTRY entries (`prompt structure`, mirror `crates/*/prompts/*.md`; `decision entries`, mirror `docs/decisions.md`; both Source::GitHead), the second after `decision log`. Add the unit tests: the y8kr joined-bullet shape, a glued bullet pair, a space-joined bullet, an intended one-line edit, a legacy mid-line phrase, a non-prompt .md file, D121/D122 inserted inside (new and in-base cases), a well-formed append, a duplicate id, a skipped id, a bad heading, no Provenance, a legacy entry untouched, a missing base, `watches` for both entries, the glob expansion, and `the_registry_declares_the_prompt_and_decision_entry_rules`. Add a path-aware base closure helper for the tests.

In crates/athena-cli/tests/mirrors.rs add `fixture` arms: PromptStructure writes `crates/demo/prompts/reader.md` (clean: unchanged or a one-line edit; drifted: bullets joined) and returns the base bytes for that path (extend the closure so the base is returned for the file the arm wrote, not only for `entry.mirror`); DecisionEntries uses base `## D01 · a` with a Provenance bullet, a clean appended D02 and a drifted D02 without Provenance. Change the loop assertions to `entry.covers(&drift.mirror)` and `drift.message.contains(&drift.mirror)`.

In crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs add `athena_source_repo_with_prompt()` (athena_source_repo plus committed `crates/demo/prompts/reader.md` and `docs/decisions.md` with two well-formed entries) and the mirrors_ tests for criterion 7 (joined bullet sent back and fixed on the send-back; decision inserted inside another sent back naming the outer entry; clean one-line prompt edit not sent back).
In run/producer.rs update the three comments (about lines 71-74, 188-192, 355-356) to list prompt files and decision entries. Make no code change.

Append D162 to docs/decisions.md after D161 (heading `## D162 · ...`, bullets Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance), with `Amends D158 in prose only: ...` at the start of the Decision bullet and no other use of amends/supersedes/superseded by. Then add the [[link]] to docs/decision-links.toml with the line of that phrase, found by Grep -n in the final file. Do not open a line with an ontology term name followed by `:`.
Add the CHANGELOG.md Unreleased `### Added` entry: root cause, both job ids, the two rules and their limits, a pointer to D162, with no claim beyond the code.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors`, `cargo test -p athena-cli` (decisions, backtest, ontology) and the full `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`; fix what fails. Do not add a test file (else add its line to xtask/shard-timings.txt).

risks.risk: False positive: a legitimate prompt edit that quotes a bullet head or writes ` - word:` in prose is sent back.
risks.mitigation: Rule (a) matches only the heads of bullets that exist in the base, and rule (b) looks only at lines not in the base and requires an alphanumeric or sentence-end character right before ` - word:`. Tests pin the legit cases: reworded bullet, reworded head, unchanged legacy mid-line phrase, a non-prompt .md file. A Grep of the current prompt files found no glued marker, so the real tree stays clean.

risks.risk: The rules do not compare against the intended edit, so a semantic mistake in a single line, or a bullet joined in a way neither rule sees (for example no colon and reworded), still reaches the verifier.
risks.mitigation: The rule is documented and named as a structure check. The CHANGELOG and D162 say that intent and the truth of changelog claims are not checked. Untrue claims and unexplained trimming (findings 2 and 3 of y8kr) are listed as out of scope.

risks.risk: Allowing a glob in `Mirror.mirror` breaks code that treats it as a file path: check_all's `is_file`, `watches`, the cli test's `put(root, entry.mirror)`.
risks.mitigation: The cli fixture arms and test assertion are in the plan (step 8). The glob only changes `check_all`, `watches` and the PromptStructure arm; the other four rules take the old path and keep their tests.

risks.risk: The link's `line` in decision-links.toml does not match the phrase line, or D162 contains a second hit, which the backtest then flags.
risks.mitigation: D162 uses exactly one `Amends D158` line and avoids `supersedes` and `superseded by`; the producer computes the link's line after the final text of the entry and re-checks it with `cargo test -p athena-cli backtest` and `decisions`.

risks.risk: D162 itself fails DecisionEntries (id, Provenance or heading shape), so the change is sent back by its own rule.
risks.mitigation: The log guard test already checks ids; the new rule checks the same. Follow D161 with D162 exactly and put the entry at the end of the file with a blank line before it.

risks.risk: The e2e fixture's commit of a prompt file or decisions.md trips another producer-step gate in the test repo (the decision gate or the scope check), so the send-back count differs.
risks.mitigation: The e2e tests build the producer's output the same way the existing mirrors_ tests do and assert on the message text. Run `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors` before the full suite.

risks.risk: Another file class (for example docs/design/*.md) can break structure the same way and is not covered.
risks.mitigation: The rule is registered as a prompts-and-log rule and is run unfiltered by the athena-cli `mirrors` test; the module doc already states that registering a mirror is prose-only. Docs files beyond these are listed in D162 as not covered.

demonstrations.method: New tests in run/tests.rs next to the existing mirrors_ tests: `mirrors_a_prompt_with_a_joined_bullet_is_sent_back_with_the_file_and_the_bullet` and `mirrors_a_decision_inserted_inside_another_is_sent_back_naming_it`, each with a fixing variant. The repo is `athena_source_repo()` plus a committed prompt file (and a committed decisions.md with Provenance). The scripted producer edits the file to the broken shape; `mirror_job` runs the whole job through `governed_job_with`, so mirror_drift_in, the one send-back and the verifier gate are the real ones. A clean one-line prompt edit is also run.
demonstrations.observes: For the broken edit: producer run count 2, the second producer prompt holds `## Sent back`, the mirror sentence, the file path, the bullet or entry id and the fix phrase, and the UI lines `producer   sent back: files kept by hand disagree`. For the fixing variant: (producer, verifier) = (2, 1) and the job lands. For the clean edit: (1, 1) with no send-back. The assertions are on the finding text, not on wiring.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new REGISTRY rules, mirror_drift_in returns nothing for the broken prompt or log: the producer count stays 1, no `## Sent back` appears in the second prompt, and the assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production flow `Athena::produce_and_verify` through the existing test harness `mirror_job(repo, extra, fix)` and `fixing_on_send_back` (exist, run/tests.rs ~2479-2513). The fake agent is the scripted `editing` script (exists) injected through `governed_job_with`. The fake only writes the broken file text; the detection is done by production code. Step 9 adds a helper `athena_source_repo_with_prompt` built from `athena_source_repo` and `commit_file` (both exist).
